title: "Background Jobs and the & Operator"

# Background Jobs and the & Operator

Appending `&` to a command forks the process into the background, returning immediate control to the script:

```bash
# Start background worker
/opt/scripts/backup.sh /var/data &
BACKUP_PID=$!
echo "Backup running in background with PID: $BACKUP_PID"

# Built-in job management (interactive or set -m)
jobs -l
```
